To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) we introduce a novel Riemann–Riemannian continuity condition that is well suited to problems with loss functions which exhibit singularities, (ii) we use this continuity condition to prove optimal regret bounds for online and stochastic optimization, (iii) we demonstrate how our theory can be applied to solve a class of inverse problems in imaging science, and (iv) we provide numerical results which validate our theory.

(1) the RL continuity condition provides a generalization of Lipschitz continuity to a wider class of optimization problems, (2) the RL condition can be used to derive optimal regret bounds for online and stochastic optimization algorithms in the presence of gradient singularities or loss function singularities, and (3) the RL condition is a useful tool for analyzing and solving a class of stochastic inverse problems arising in imaging science.

we have extended the theory of online and stochastic gradient descent to the setting of Riemann–Liapunov continuity, a generalization of Lipschitz continuity, which allows us to handle loss functions that exhibit singularities or are singular themselves.
the Riemannian framework allows us to study online and stochastic optimization with loss functions that exhibit gradient singularities and/or are singular themselves.

the RL continuity condition is a natural and effective framework for the analysis of optimization problems with non-Lipschitz continuous loss functions.
the Riemannian framework can provide a unified approach to the design of algorithms for a variety of online and stochastic problems that exhibit singularities.
